title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: choose file extensions from a curated list
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's planned rollout, the effect on edited policies and the alternative for unsupported files. Minor corrections should complete the documented control route and remove a checklist instruction whose control is missing from the table.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans a pre-curated file extension picker for the Endpoint DLP file extension condition.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP now includes a pre curated list of file extensions for the file extension condition.

claims.claim: Previously, free-form entry could allow unsupported or non-scannable extensions.
claims.quote: Previously, file extensions were entered as free form text, which could result in unsupported or non-scannable extensions being used.

claims.claim: The roadmap says unsupported or non-scannable extensions could leave gaps in protection.
claims.quote: This could lead to gaps in protection and increase processing overhead on endpoints.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes reduced unnecessary endpoint processing without quantifying the improvement.
claims.quote: This helps improve policy reliability and reduces unnecessary processing on endpoints.

claims.claim: Only supported, scannable file types will appear in the picker.
claims.quote: Only file types that are supported and can be scanned appear in the picker.

claims.claim: Free-form file extension entry will no longer be available.
claims.quote: Free-form text entry for file extensions is no longer available.

claims.claim: No tenant UI or automation switch to retain free-form entry or disable the picker is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP pre curated file extension list tenant disable opt out PowerShell. Opened Configure endpoint data loss prevention settings, New-DlpComplianceRule, Set-DlpComplianceRule and Set-PolicyConfig; no documented picker opt-out.

claims.claim: The cited portal route starts Data Loss Prevention > Policies > Enterprise applications & devices > Create policy > Custom > Custom policy.
claims.quote: Open Data Loss Prevention > Policies. ... Select Enterprise applications & devices. ... Select Create policy and select the Custom from the Categories then Custom policy template from Regulations.
claims.fix: Complete the path as 'Data Loss Prevention > Policies > Enterprise applications & devices > Create policy > Categories > Custom > Regulations > Custom policy > Admin units > Full directory > Devices > rule > Actions > Audit or restrict activities on devices > Apply restrictions to specific activity > Apply restrictions to only unsupported file extensions'. Keep the Document could not be scanned condition in the note. The cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-files-edlp-doesnt-scan supports this route; note that the also-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-sharing-set-unsupported-files instead puts Create policy before Enterprise applications & devices.

claims.claim: The continuation uses Full directory, Devices and a rule with Document could not be scanned and the unsupported-file action.
claims.quote: Select Full directory under Admin units. ... Scope the location to Devices only. ... Select Document could not be scanned. ... Select Audit or restrict activities on devices. ... Select Apply restrictions to only unsupported file extensions.

claims.claim: No equivalent automation operation for the Apply restrictions to only unsupported file extensions option is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP "Apply restrictions to only unsupported file extensions" "PowerShell"; EndpointDlpRestrictions unsupported file extensions setting PowerShell Set-DlpComplianceRule. Read New-/Set-DlpComplianceRule and Set-PolicyConfig; no documented setting for this option.

claims.claim: Unsupported file extension exclusions is a separate Endpoint DLP setting that excludes extensions from unsupported-file policy coverage.
claims.quote: Because this condition can potentially include many unsupported file extensions, refine detection by adding unsupported extensions to exclude.
